text.p: These are leading stories in this morning's Paris newspapers.
LES ECHOS
-- Suez board favours merger project with Lyonnaise des Eaux.
-- Finance Ministry confirms its 2.3 percent growth forecast for 1997.
-- Danone chairman Franck Riboud says does not plan to sell beer or packaging activities in the near term.
LA TRIBUNE
-- Suez shareholders to receive an exceptional 3.4 billion franc dividend as part of plans to merge with Lyonnaise des Eaux.
-- French new car sales plunge by some 21 percent in March from year-earlier levels, mainly due to sales of smaller cars.
-- Britain's GEC may have submitted a bid for Thomson-CSF, government to examine offers on Friday and decide which are valid.
-- Ministers do not agree on plans to recapitalise arms manufacturer GIAT Industries.
L'AGEFI
-- Minority shareholders expected to seize the opportunity created by merger projects with Lyonnaise des Eaux to sell their stakes in Suez.
-- OFCE expects economic pickup to confirm in 1997 and widen in 1998.
-- Lagardere expected to post a one-billion-franc net profit for 1996.
LE FIGARO-ECONOMIE
-- Ground staff at Air France Europe to strike for fifth day today against process of planned merger with Air France.
LIBERATION (Economic section)
-- France Telecom studies projects to offer to sell equity to some 1,000 executive through stock-option plans to be detailed in September.
THE INTERNATIONAL HERALD TRIBUNE
-- Suez board approves plans to merge with Lyonnaise des Eaux.
